info.title: hotel-drogon implemented account API
info.description: Observed Phase 1 contract for existing Drogon routes only. This does not specify registration, password reset, remember-me, an account React journey, or a verified staff second factor. Error bodies and cookie behavior reflect the current handlers, including their limitations.

servers.description: Same origin as the React application

options.summary: Return an empty success for the login route's explicit OPTIONS handler

post.description: No CSRF token is required to log in. Missing username or password in a valid JSON object returns 401. Authentication system errors are also currently mapped to 401; a banned user receives 403.

options.summary: Return an empty success for the staff-login route's explicit OPTIONS handler

post.description: No public session or CSRF token is required by this handler. Rank below 5 returns 403. The current code does not verify an enrolled TOTP secret: an omitted code is marked verified, a nonempty six-character code is marked verified, and another nonempty length still returns 200 with 2fa_verified=false. This response must not be treated as proof of real second-factor authentication or staff release readiness. Authentication failures, including a ban or service error, are mapped to 401 here.

Requires a session-bound CSRF token. The handler returns 200 and clears hotel_session and XSRF-TOKEN even if deleting the Redis key reports failure. It does not clear hotel_staff_session. The CSRF filter runs before the handler, so a missing token or unusable public session returns 403.

get.summary: Read the signed-in user's current profile
get.description: The public hotel_session cookie is required. The response reads the current PolarIS user row rather than only the session snapshot. A missing or expired session returns 401. A missing row, or a database lookup failure currently collapsed to no row, returns 404.

post.description: The handler requires a JSON string, trims surrounding whitespace, and rejects a value longer than 127 characters with 400 and the legacy profile.php notice "Invalid profile details." An earlier revision truncated to 128 bytes instead; that silently changed legacy behaviour and could cut a multibyte motto mid-character, so it was corrected rather than documented as the contract.

post.summary: Update the current user's avatar look and gender
post.description: The handler requires a JSON string for look, trims surrounding whitespace, and rejects a value longer than 255 characters with 400. The bound is 255 rather than legacy profile.php's 256 because PolarIS `users.look` is `varchar(255)`: a 256-character figure cannot be stored, so the handler refuses it explicitly instead of letting the write fail. gender is optional; when supplied it must be exactly M or F (the column is an enum of those two), otherwise the request is rejected with the legacy notice. An earlier revision stored any string and coerced an invalid gender to M, which legacy profile.php never did.
The current handler accepts any JSON string containing @; it does not perform full email validation. A successful update sets mail_verified to false.

The handler checks that both keys are present and that new_password has at least six bytes, then re-authenticates with current_password. On success the existing public session remains valid. Password reset and reauthentication routes are not implemented in this API slice.

get.summary: Read the signed-in user's Coin, Pixel and Point balances
get.description: The converted `credits.php` purse block. Reads the live PolarIS `users` row rather than summing the ledger: the row is the balance of record, and the ledger only records what the website itself changed, so a balance derived from it would disagree with the emulator. Takes no user id — the subject is always the session's own user. 401 without a usable public session; 404 when the session is valid but the row is gone.

get.summary: Read the signed-in user's own transaction ledger
get.description: The converted `history.php`: the caller's rows from `phpretro_transactions`, newest first with `id` as the tiebreak, capped at 100. The query is scoped by the session's user id and the route accepts no user parameter, so another account's ledger is not reachable through it. An empty `items` array is the normal answer on a stack whose ledger was never written: only the housekeeping credit adjustment and the MyHabbo Homes store write rows, and neither is ported yet.

post.summary: Restore a session from the remember-me cookie
post.description: The consume side of remember-me. Legacy had no route for this: `core.php` redirected a request that was anonymous but carried the cookies to `/security_check_token`, a rewrite of `security_check.php?type=token`. A decoupled SPA has no server-side redirect to hook, so the client calls this when it finds itself signed out while holding a token. It requires BOTH cookies — `rememberme` must be the string "true" and `rememberme_token` must be present — which is the legacy front-controller condition; a stray token without its flag does nothing. Only the SHA-256 digest of the token is compared, because `users.remember_token_hash` stores the digest and never the token. The lookup requires `remember_token_expires_at` to be strictly in the future, and a banned account is refused, as `HoloUser::loginFromToken` did. **The session it creates always carries `reauth_required: true`** and the token is cleared, so a token restores a session but never grants entry to the hotel on its own — the holder must still prove the password at `/api/account/reauthenticate`. No CSRF token is required: this creates a session rather than acting inside one, exactly like login.

post.summary: Request a password reset link for an account
post.description: The converted `forgot.php` `actionForgot`. The account must match on BOTH username and email exactly, with `mail_verified = '1'` — legacy's own predicate, condition for condition. On a match a single-use token is generated, stored in Redis only as a SHA-256 hash under `password_reset:<hash>` with a 30-minute TTL, and sent to the account's own address; no column is added to a PolarIS table because PolarIS has none for this. **No mail transport exists in this stack**, so delivery is the log-only transport and the message is recorded rather than sent; the response does not distinguish that, and must not be read as proof an email arrived. Unlike legacy, every outcome answers with the same 200 and the same text: legacy's distinct "Invalid details." turned the form into an oracle for which accounts exist. Carries `CsrfPublicFilter`, not `CsrfFilter`, because the caller has no session for a session-bound token to be validated against; the filter requires the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header, which a cross-origin request cannot set without a preflight this application does not answer.

post.summary: Spend a reset token and set a new password
post.description: There is no legacy equivalent: `forgot.php` mailed a plaintext password and had no second step. The token is consumed with Redis `GETDEL`, so it is single-use even under concurrent requests — exactly one caller can see the stored value. An unknown, expired or already-spent token all answer 401 with the same message, so a caller cannot probe which tokens exist. A password shorter than six bytes answers 400, the same floor the authenticated change route enforces, so a reset cannot produce a password that route would refuse. Also carries `CsrfPublicFilter`: the token in the body is the primary control, and the header requirement is a second, weaker one.

post.summary: List the account names registered to an email address
post.description: The converted `forgot.php` `actionList`. Legacy mailed the list; there is no mail transport here, so the names are returned in the response instead and `mail_transport` says `log-only` so no caller implies an email was sent. Legacy did not require the address to be verified for this action and neither does this: it discloses only names the requester already has the address for, and it is the documented recovery path for a forgotten username. Carries `CsrfPublicFilter` for the same no-session reason as the other two.

get.summary: Report what the current session may do
get.description: Carries the legacy `$_SESSION['reauthenticate']` flag as `reauth_required`. Legacy set it when a session was established from a remember-me token rather than a fresh password, and `client.php` refused to open the hotel until the password was proved again. The flag lives in the Redis session document, so it is server state a client cannot forge. 401 without a usable public session.

post.summary: Prove the account password and clear the step-up requirement
post.description: The converted `reauthenticate.php`. Re-runs the full credential check through the same service method login uses, so a password that would not pass login cannot pass step-up, then clears the flag in the Redis session. A correct password that cannot be recorded because the session update failed answers 500 rather than 200: reporting success would let the client believe a step-up happened that did not. CSRF-filtered normally — this caller has a session, so a session-bound token exists and there is no reason to accept less.

post.summary: Rotate the caller's SSO ticket and report client launch options
post.description: The converted `client.php` handoff. A CSRF-protected POST writes only the caller's `users.auth_ticket` with a fresh legacy-format ticket and an audit entry. `octane_url` is a validated loopback-only development client origin; an empty value means it is not configured. `handoff_ready` means this origin or the legacy hotel host and port are configured. `handoff_available` also requires a stored ticket. These are website-side facts; only an emulator login proves acceptance. The ticket is passed to Octane in a query string required by that client, so it may appear in browser history and client-side access logs. The pinned emulator consumes the ticket at game login but restores it during disconnect grace and does not enforce an expiry for a website-issued ticket; production Octane launch remains blocked pending a replay bound.

userSession.name: hotel_session
userSession.description: Opaque public-session token in a Redis-backed session, issued by login. A separate hotel_staff_session is not sufficient for these account routes.

CsrfHeader.name: X-XSRF-TOKEN
CsrfHeader.description: Required for a successful mutation unless the same session-bound token is supplied as JSON csrf_token or a form/query csrf_token parameter. The login response and readable XSRF-TOKEN cookie supply its value. The filter checks the submitted token against the Redis public session and runs before account authorization.

CsrfPublicHeader.name: X-XSRF-TOKEN
CsrfPublicHeader.description: Required by `CsrfPublicFilter` for the pre-authentication routes, which have no session for `CsrfFilter` to validate a token against. The filter checks PRESENCE only, not the value: there is nothing to compare it to before a session exists. What makes that meaningful is that a cross-origin request cannot set a custom header without a CORS preflight this application does not answer. Do not mistake this for token validation.

totp_code.description: Accepted by current code but not validated against an enrolled secret.

motto.description: Trimmed before storage; longer than 127 characters is rejected with 400.

look.description: Trimmed before storage; longer than 255 characters is rejected with 400 because users.look is varchar(255).

gender.description: Optional. Must be exactly M or F when supplied; anything else is rejected with 400.

email.description: Only an @ character is checked by the current handler.

new_password.description: At least six bytes according to the current handler.

2fa_verified.description: Current implementation's flag, not proof of an enrolled-secret challenge.

type.description: Ledger row kind. The two the legacy writers produce are admin_grant (housekeeping credit adjustment) and homes_store (MyHabbo store purchase).

reference_id.description: Empty when the column is NULL; the schema allows NULL.

limit.description: The server's page cap (100, as history.php used).

message.description: One text for every outcome, so the response cannot be used to test whether an account exists.

token.description: The single-use token from the reset link.

new_password.description: At least six bytes, matching the authenticated change route's floor.

mail_transport.description: log-only when no transport is configured, so a caller does not imply an email was sent. smtp is not reachable today.

reauth_required.description: The legacy $_SESSION['reauthenticate'] flag: this session must prove the password before entering the hotel.
Always true for a token-established session. This is the legacy design: the token restores the session and the password is still required before entering the hotel.

handoff_ready.description: A validated Octane origin or legacy hotel host and port are configured.

handoff_available.description: handoff_ready AND the SSO ticket was stored. Emulator acceptance is separate.

octane_url.description: Validated Octane origin ending in a slash, or empty when unconfigured.

sso_ticket.description: Legacy 8-4-4-4-12 lowercase-hex ticket, also stored in users.auth_ticket. Empty when storing failed.

missing_settings.description: phpretro_site_settings keys that are absent or empty.

notes.description: Plain statement of what the handoff does and does not claim.

LoginSuccess.description: Public session created. Two Set-Cookie headers: hotel_session is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, Max-Age=604800; XSRF-TOKEN is readable by JavaScript, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, Max-Age=604800. The handlers do not set Secure.

Set-Cookie.description: hotel_session and XSRF-TOKEN are sent as separate header fields.

StaffLoginSuccess.description: Separate staff session created. Set-Cookie hotel_staff_session is HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/, Max-Age=7200. The handler does not set Secure.

LogoutSuccess.description: Public cookies cleared using Max-Age=0; the staff cookie is unchanged.

MeSuccess.description: Current user and session CSRF token.

EmailSuccess.description: Stored email with mail_verified reset to false.

PurseSuccess.description: Balances read from the live PolarIS users row.

TransactionsSuccess.description: The caller's own ledger page, newest first. items may be empty.

ClientEntrySuccess.description: A fresh SSO ticket plus the connection settings, and an explicit statement of whether a handoff is available.

ForgotPasswordNeutral.description: One neutral message for every outcome.

ForgotUsernameSuccess.description: The account names on the supplied address, and which transport was used.

SessionStateSuccess.description: The session's user and whether step-up is required.

ReauthenticateSuccess.description: The password matched and the step-up flag is cleared.

InvalidResetToken.description: The token is unknown, expired or already spent — one answer for all three.

PublicCsrfForbidden.description: The X-XSRF-TOKEN header was absent. The value is not checked; see the CsrfPublicHeader parameter.

ReauthFlagFailure.description: The password was correct but the session flag could not be cleared, so the step-up did not take effect.

RememberLoginSuccess.description: Session restored from the remember-me token; step-up is now required. Clears the rememberme and rememberme_token cookies because the token has been spent, and sets hotel_session and XSRF-TOKEN.

Set-Cookie.description: hotel_session and XSRF-TOKEN issued; rememberme and rememberme_token cleared.

RememberTokenInvalid.description: No usable token: absent, unknown, expired, already spent, or sent without the rememberme flag cookie. Both cookies are cleared.

StepUpFailure.description: The token was valid but the session could not be marked as requiring step-up, so it was destroyed rather than issued unprivileged-by-accident.

InvalidJson.description: JSON body could not be read.

Unauthorized.description: Invalid credentials or missing/expired public session, depending on route.

Banned.description: Public login refused for a banned user; body also contains ban_reason and ban_expires.

CsrfForbidden.description: CSRF token missing, no active session, or token mismatch. The CSRF filter runs before account handlers.

BadRequestOrUpdateFailure.description: Request validation or database update failed; the body message distinguishes them.

UserNotFound.description: User row unavailable after valid session; current service also maps a lookup failure here.

SessionFailure.description: Redis session creation failed after valid credentials.
